data.name: Docs_CatalogLead
data.value: Connect OpenRussiaRouter to popular AI development and automation tools. Every tool uses a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint and your API key.

data.name: Docs_ClaudeCode_Hero
data.value: Claude Code — Anthropic's terminal agent, connected to OpenRussiaRouter through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint

data.name: Docs_ClaudeCode_Short
data.value: Anthropic's terminal agent — edits code, runs commands and git operations.

data.name: Docs_ClaudeCode_Way1Desc
data.value: Install Claude Code and set environment variables before launch. The client will pick them up automatically.

data.name: Docs_ClaudeCode_Way2Code
data.value:
pip install 'litellm[proxy]'
cat > litellm.yaml <<EOF model_list: - model_name: openrussiarouter litellm_params: model: openai/{MODEL_ID} api_base: "{BASE_URL}" api_key: "sk-orr-xxx" EOF
litellm --config litellm.yaml --port 4000

data.name: Docs_ClaudeCode_Way2Desc
data.value: Run a local LiteLLM proxy that translates the Anthropic format into OpenAI-chat and point Claude Code at it.

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Hero
data.value: Hermes Agent — open-source autonomous agent by Nous Research with memory and 21+ messengers, connected to OpenRussiaRouter

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Short
data.value: Open-source autonomous agent with persistent memory and 21+ messengers.

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Way1Desc
data.value: Run the built-in wizard: pick Custom endpoint, set the base URL, paste the API key and choose a default model.

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Way2Code
data.value: hermes config set OPENAI_API_KEY sk-orr-xxx hermes config set model.provider custom hermes config set model.base_url {BASE_URL} hermes config set model.default <paste-a-model-id>

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Way2Desc
data.value: If you already have a key and want to skip the wizard — these four commands set every option at once.

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Way3Code
data.value:
# ~/.hermes/.env OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-orr-xxx
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml custom_providers: - name: openrussiarouter base_url: {BASE_URL} key_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY api_mode: chat_completions
model: default: <paste-a-model-id> provider: custom:openrussiarouter

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Way3Desc
data.value: A named provider is convenient when you switch between several APIs — change only the `custom:NAME/MODEL` part in commands.

data.name: Docs_KiloCode_Hero
data.value: Kilo Code — AI agent inside VS Code, connected to OpenRussiaRouter through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint

data.name: Docs_KiloCode_Short
data.value: AI agent in VS Code — writes and edits code, chats in a side panel, works with any model.

data.name: Docs_KiloCode_Way1Desc
data.value: In the extension settings, add a new OpenAI-compatible provider and set the base URL plus API key. If your Kilo Code UI labels differ, match the fields by their purpose — baseUrl / apiKey / api=openai-chat.

data.name: Docs_Lead
data.value: Connect to OpenRussiaRouter with an OpenAI-compatible request flow. Point any OpenAI client at the endpoint below and authenticate with your API key.

data.name: Docs_ListModels
data.value: List models available to your account

data.name: Docs_OpenClaw_Hero
data.value: OpenClaw — open-source AI agent for messengers, connected to OpenRussiaRouter

data.name: Docs_OpenClaw_Short
data.value: Open-source AI agent for Telegram, Discord and Slack — models through a single API key.

data.name: Docs_OpenClaw_Way1Desc
data.value: Open `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` and add the `models.providers.openrussiarouter` block. The `api: openai-completions` flag switches to OpenAI-chat mode.

data.name: Docs_StepBuyDesc
data.value: Add USD balance once and use it across available models.

data.name: Docs_StepKeyDesc
data.value: Create an API key in the workspace and use it as a bearer token.

data.name: Docs_StepModelDesc
data.value: Open the model catalog and copy the public model ID you want to use.

data.name: Docs_StepSignupDesc
data.value: Create your account and open the workspace.

data.name: Docs_Tool_AnthropicNote
data.value: Limitation. Claude Code sends requests in Anthropic format (`/v1/messages`) by default. Our gateway accepts OpenAI-chat (`/v1/chat/completions`). Direct connection works if the client supports an OpenAI preset — for guaranteed compatibility, run a LiteLLM proxy that translates between the formats.

data.name: Docs_Tool_GetApiKey
data.value: Open the API keys section and create a new key. It starts with `sk-orr-`.

data.name: Docs_Tool_GetBaseUrl
data.value: Copy this address — you will need it when configuring the client.

data.name: Docs_Tool_Verify
data.value: Run the request below — if a list of models comes back, the connection works.

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Caveat1
data.value: Hermes requires models with at least 64K tokens of context — pick a model with a sufficiently large window.

data.name: Docs_Hermes_Caveat2
data.value: If you leave the default provider (OpenRouter), the agent will look for `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Switch `model.provider` to `custom` or `custom:openrussiarouter`.

data.name: Docs_OpenClaw_Caveat1
data.value: Model format in OpenClaw commands is `openrussiarouter/<paste-a-model-id>`. The provider prefix is required.

data.name: Docs_OpenClaw_Caveat2
data.value: For production, use named providers with `fallbacks` so the agent keeps working when one model is unavailable.

data.name: Docs_KiloCode_Caveat1
data.value: Field names in Kilo Code settings depend on the extension version. If the UI looks different, match by purpose: `baseUrl`, `apiKey`, `api=openai-chat`.

data.name: Docs_KiloCode_Caveat2
data.value: After changing the provider, restart VS Code — otherwise Kilo Code keeps using the old endpoint.

data.name: Docs_ClaudeCode_Caveat1
data.value: Claude Code sends requests in Anthropic format (`/v1/messages`) by default. Our gateway accepts OpenAI-chat only. Use a LiteLLM proxy for guaranteed compatibility.

data.name: Docs_ClaudeCode_Caveat2
data.value: If the client supports an OpenAI preset through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, try direct connection — but be ready for request-format errors.
